title: Rovia internal control response
description: What the extension returns from PacketTunnelProvider.handleAppMessage. The request contract is schemas/control-api.schema.json; this file is the other half of the same exchange, so a response cannot carry a field the request contract does not define and a caller can tell a result from a refusal without guessing. The envelope is closed: an unknown field is a contract change, not a forward-compatible extra.

apiVersion.description: The control API version this build speaks.

requestID.description: The identifier from the request, or the literal 'unknown' when the request could not be parsed far enough to read one.

ok.description: Whether the method ran. An ok response carries result and no error; a refusal carries error and no result.

result.description: The only result this build can produce. status.get is the only implemented method, so the payload is the status envelope; a method that returns data will add its own closed shape and a probe here rather than widening this one.

state.description: A non-empty state name from the tunnel lifecycle: disconnected, connecting, connected, disconnecting, idle, failed, or unavailable. The set is a bounded string rather than an enum so the lifecycle can grow without a schema change.

errorCode.description: The closed set of refusals. A refusal carries a stable code, never a message, so nothing from the request or the device can echo back into the response.
